title: Abstraction Layers Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Computational Thinking
Abstraction
Custom Blocks
Scratch
description: A student peels back the layers of an abstraction. A detail-level slider opens one named block, draw flower, into three blocks and then into eight machine steps, and a checkbox shows how many things there are to remember at each layer.

learningObjectives: Explain that naming a group of steps hides detail without removing it.
State how many underlying steps a single named block stands for.
prerequisites: Decomposition: a big job is made of smaller jobs

controls.label: Detail level
controls.description: How many layers of detail are showing

controls.label: Show step count
controls.description: Shows how many things there are to remember in each band

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns the slider to 1 and turns the step count off

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through reveal: the student predicts what a name hides, then opens one layer at a time
keyQuestions: How many steps are hiding inside the name draw flower?
When you slide back to level 1, did the steps go away?
Why is one name easier to think about than eight steps?
commonMisconceptions: Abstraction deletes the details. It only hides them; the computer still does every step.
A shorter description is missing something. It means the same steps under a name.
assessmentOpportunities: Ask the student to predict the number of hidden steps before moving the slider.
Have the student write a name and its hidden steps for an everyday job.
